recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say where the third vertex is, and how that shortens the area formula.

steps.label: Find the points of intersection
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Both lines of the pair pass through the ORIGIN, so O is automatically the third vertex. Substitute the line into the pair to find where the other two vertices sit.
lines: First we find the points of intersection of  3x² − 4xy + y² = 0  ……(1)  and  2x − y = 6  ……(2)

recall.must_convey: That the line is rearranged as y = 2x − 6 ready to substitute into the pair.
accept: rearrange the line to make y the subject then substitute into the pair
y is two x minus six
both lines of the pair pass through the origin so that is one vertex
line ni y ki solve chesi pair lo substitute cheyyali
find where the line meets the pair
heard_as: y equals two x minus six

steps.why: A homogeneous second-degree equation always represents two lines through the ORIGIN, so one vertex is free — that is what makes both the centroid and the area short to compute.
common_mistakes: Trying to factorise the pair before substituting, which is more work.
Forgetting that the origin is a vertex.

steps.label: Solve for both vertices
steps.margin_note: First mark. Substituting collapses the pair to a single quadratic in x, and its two roots give the two vertices.
lines: ∴ A point of intersection is A = (6, 6)
⇒ the other point of intersection is B = (−6, −18)
Also the pair of lines 3x² − 4xy + y² = 0 intersect at O(0, 0)

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives x² = 36, so the vertices are A(6, 6), B(−6, −18) and O(0, 0).
accept: substitute and solve the quadratic to get x equals plus or minus six
the two vertices are six comma six and minus six comma minus eighteen
the third vertex is the origin
substitute chesthe x square equals thirty six vasthundi
all three vertices

steps.why: The x terms cancel almost entirely, leaving x² = 36 — the numbers in this question were chosen so the quadratic has no linear term.
common_mistakes: Taking only the positive root and finding one vertex.

steps.label: Find the centroid
steps.margin_note: One mark. The centroid is the plain average of the three vertices. With the origin among them, two of the six numbers are zero.
lines: ∴ The centroid of the triangle formed by O(0,0), A(6, 6), B(−6, −18) is

recall.must_convey: That averaging the three vertices gives the centroid (0, −4).
accept: the centroid is the average of the three vertices
add the x's and divide by three, same for the y's
the centroid is zero comma minus four
moodu vertices average teesukovali
centroid is zero minus four

steps.why: The centroid needs all three vertices, unlike the area, which can be written from two when the third is the origin.
common_mistakes: Averaging only the two non-origin vertices.

steps.label: Find the area
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. With one vertex at the origin the area determinant collapses to ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| — only the two other vertices appear.

lines.text: ∴ Area = 36 sq.units,  and the centroid is (0, −4)

recall.must_convey: That the area is ½|x₁y₂ − x₂y₁| = ½|−72| = 36 sq.units.
accept: the area with a vertex at the origin is half mod x one y two minus x two y one
six times minus eighteen minus minus six times six
the area is thirty six square units
origin vertex unnappudu area formula chinnadi
area is thirty six

steps.why: The modulus is what keeps the area positive — the determinant itself comes out negative here, which says only that the vertices were listed clockwise.
common_mistakes: Reporting the area as −36 by dropping the modulus.
Using all three vertices in a determinant and mis-expanding it.
